records.issue_text: [BUG] In reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey(), the webauthn-form absence check wraps assertThat(..., nullValue()) inside try { ... fail(...) } catch (Exception nsee), which makes both branches pass and the fail() unreachable. The assertion is dead: if the //form[@id='webauth'] element IS present (findElement succeeds), assertThat throws AssertionError which is swallowed by catch(Exception) and the test silently passes; if the element is absent, findElement throws NoSuchElementException which is also swallowed. The 'passkeys should not be shown during re-authentication' guarantee the test claims to verify is never actually verified, so a regression that shows the passkey button ships undetected.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] UsernameForm.authenticate calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only definition added in this diff is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in UsernamePasswordForm — no no-arg overload is introduced in UsernameForm or AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, so this call does not resolve to any method shown in this diff. Either the diff is missing the UsernameForm-side implementation entirely (the browser flow's UsernameForm execution then relies on undefined behavior) or the gating logic lives out-of-diff and cannot be verified as consistent with the UsernamePasswordForm version; the two call sites are already drifting (one takes a user, one takes none), so the next change to passkey gating must be made twice.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The refactor inverts fillContextForm's gating from "user is not already selected" to "shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators", and the base implementation returns true only when the user is already set — meaning the identified-authenticators branch is now only reachable when a user exists, while the anonymous/conditional-UI path (user == null) relies on the not-identified branch being correct for it. records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] During re-authentication (context.getUser() != null) with conditional passkeys enabled, the username form is now rendered instead of being skipped, and no code in this diff verifies that the user re-submitted to the form matches the user already set in the authentication context. An attacker (or anyone at a shared kiosk) triggering prompt=login on a flow that uses UsernameForm can submit a different username during re-authentication and complete the flow as that other account, silently substituting the re-authenticated user for the user the client expected to re-verify; operators relying on prompt=login as a proof of continued possession of the original user's session lose that guarantee.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The try/catch pattern in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey (`MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")), nullValue()); fail("Not expected to have webauthn button"); } catch (Exception nsee)`) is a false-confidence construct: driver.findElement never returns null, so the assertThat(nullValue()) branch can never pass, and the blanket `catch (Exception)` swallows every RuntimeException including WebDriverException/StaleElementReferenceException, so the test passes whenever findElement throws for any reason — a page-render error is indistinguishable from correct element absence. A regression that breaks the login page rendering entirely (findElement fails with a non-NoSuchElementException) is reported as a PASS of 'webauthn elements not available', giving false confidence that the passkeys-disabled behavior is verified; the correct assertion would be assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) as the sibling tests use.
